lesson.title: Specify logging and distinguish retention rules
lesson.summary: Distinguish automatic logging capability from controlled-log custody.

prerequisites.reason: Provider custody is an actor-specific obligation.
Relevant events support lifecycle risk management.

blocks: **Logging capability** means the system technically allows automatic recording of events over its lifetime. Logs are event records that support appropriate traceability for its intended purpose.

Article 12 connects relevant events to identifying Article 79 risk situations or substantial modification, post-market monitoring and deployer operation monitoring. It does not require storing every event indefinitely.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 12(1), (2), 19; Articles 3(23), 79(1)

blocks: An **Article 79 risk** includes the specified health/safety or fundamental-rights concerns addressed by that provision. A **substantial modification** is a post-supply change not foreseen or planned in the initial assessment which affects system-requirement compliance or changes the assessed intended purpose.
These are triggers to inspect, not labels for every minor edit. Northbridge should be able to record events relevant to unexpected operation and meaningful changes.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 12(1), (2), 19; Articles 3(23), 79(1)

blocks: **Controlled-log retention** concerns automatically generated logs to the extent under the provider’s control. Article 19 requires a purpose-appropriate period of at least six months unless applicable Union/national law provides otherwise, especially personal-data law.
This is a qualified minimum, not a command to collect unlimited personal data. Separate which actor controls which records, the period and the other-law basis.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 12(1), (2), 19; Articles 3(23), 79(1)

blocks: Financial institutions covered by the specified Union financial-law governance rules maintain these logs as part of the relevant financial documentation. Specialist remote-identification fields are taught in the optional biometric lesson.

Case: Northbridge’s feature can log events, but no one can identify where controlled logs are retained. Capability alone does not prove custody. Conversely, a stored launch report does not demonstrate lifetime automatic logging.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 12(1), (2), 19; Articles 3(23), 79(1)

questions.prompt: Northbridge stores a launch report but its system cannot automatically log operational events. What is missing?

options.blocks: Automatic event recording across system lifetime
options.reason: Capability is separate from static documentation.
A brochure does not implement event recording.

options.blocks: A rule to retain all events forever
options.reason: Lifetime capability is not perpetual retention.

questions.prompt: Northbridge says the six-month rule applies only to logs another actor exclusively controls. What should the assessor check?

options.blocks: Only logs exclusively controlled by someone else
Every record globally regardless of control
Automatically generated logs to the extent under its control
options.reason: Control determines this actor’s custody boundary.

variants.prompt: Which logs does the provider custody duty concern?

options.blocks: Every record globally regardless of control
Automatically generated logs to the extent under its control
options.reason: Control determines this actor’s custody boundary.

options.blocks: Only logs exclusively controlled by someone else

questions.prompt: A retention policy states “six months regardless of any applicable law.” Is that complete?

options.blocks: Indefinitely because logging works for life
options.reason: Capability and custody periods are distinct.

options.blocks: Appropriate period, normally at least six months, with other-law qualifications
options.reason: The statutory rule preserves applicable contrary law.

options.blocks: Exactly six months with no exceptions
options.reason: The minimum and qualifications are different.
